editorial_conventions: Features X and target y are distinct; supervised learning includes regression and classification.
Logistic regression uses probabilistic log loss in the examples; squared distance to a separating line is not its standard likelihood objective.
Averaging or voting is not synonymous with boosting, and ensembles do not guarantee improvement.
Training, hyperparameter validation and final holdout are separate; preprocessing is fitted only within training data. Financial observations retain temporal order and label-availability constraints.
PCA creates component features and does not by itself select original columns or identify economic causes.
Graph layout position is not a centrality measure or evidence of causal influence.

The course portfolio lab explicitly uses the same training and evaluation dates; original public examples use a held-out period. Buy-and-hold drift can change realized portfolio moments independently of skewness or kurtosis.
A historical T-bill quote is not automatically a realized weekly risk-free return. Borrowing/lending and cash-volatility assumptions are stated explicitly.
Solver success is checked alongside feasibility; a success flag alone is not a proof of global optimality for arbitrary objectives.
example_scope: Original fixed hypothetical fixtures and seeded simulations. All displayed numerical results are computed from these fixtures, not empirical market performance.
